Executive Director

Location: San Francisco Bay Area, CA

Position Type: Full\-Time, Approx. 60% On\-Site \& Community Presence / 40% Development \& Strategic Partnerships

Reports To: Board of Directors

About the Organization

Rooted directly in our local neighborhood, we are a community\-focused social services agency dedicated to building community resilience by addressing food insecurity, navigating housing options, teaching personal finance, coaching career opportunities, training on overdose recognition and response.

Position Overview

We are seeking a passionate, community\-grounded Executive Director to lead our agency into its next chapter of impact. As the leader of a nimble organization comprised of full\- and part\-time staff plus volunteers, the Executive Director is a hands\-on leader who bridges strategic vision with direct community connection.

The ideal candidate blends strong grant\-writing skills with deep field experience. You will spend roughly 60% of your time on\-site and in the neighborhood—working alongside staff, volunteers, and clients—and 40% of your time cultivating donors, securing grant opportunities, and building strategic alliances across the San Francisco Bay Area.

Key ResponsibilitiesStrategic Fundraising \& Resource Development

* Lead fundraising initiatives to establish a diversified, broad donor base to maintain and, over time, grow the agency’s operating budget
* Identify, apply for, and manage grant opportunities using grant management platforms
* With assistance from Board members, cultivate relationships with local philanthropic foundations, family trusts, and individual donors throughout the Bay Area
* Partner closely with the Board of Directors on stewardship and community outreach

Operational Leadership \& Organizational Culture

* Provide supportive, transparent leadership to a small team of full\-time and part\-time staff and community volunteers across all core initiatives
* Foster an internal environment built on trust, safety, and clear communication to strengthen the agency's human fabric
* Manage staff operational capacity and develop service delivery skills and operational workflows
* Lead organizational development initiatives including staff training, team management strategies, and program expansion efforts
* Ensure financial sustainability, sound budget management, and operational compliance

Organizational Partnerships \& Stakeholder Engagement

* Build strong collaborative partnerships with local organizations (e.g., food distribution partners, faith\-based organizations, and university social work programs) to align service delivery with community needs and identify joint funding streams
* Establish effective working relationships with city and county jurisdictions across the Bay Area (e.g., public health, homelessness, food security, child care, and violence prevention agencies)
* Act as the primary spokesperson and advocate for the agency and the surrounding neighborhood

Program Oversight and Management

* Direct food pantry operations and logistics
* Maintain an up\-to\-date grant application calendar that is shared regularly with the Board for review
* Oversee day\-to\-day operations and ensure staff members are effectively completing their job duties and providing high\-quality service to the community
* Manage program execution in compliance with grant requirements, including filing reports in a timely manner with grantors
* Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations pertaining to social services agencies
* Manage the operating budget and monitor financial health, ensure proper resource allocation aligned with organizational goals

Qualifications and Experience

* Degree in Social Work (BSW/MSW) or Public Policy (MPP/MPA) required
* Minimum of 12 years relevant experience working within a social services non\-profit agency, of which at least 3 years must have been in a senior role (e.g., Executive Director, Associate Executive Director, Chief Program Officer)
* Knowledge of legal regulations governing social services agencies
* Multiple years of hands\-on experience working directly with clients experiencing poverty, homelessness, crisis, or food insecurity.
* Demonstrated supervisory experience in managing social service program staff
* Experience with online grant management platforms systems
* Familiarity with Bay Area city and county agencies including violence prevention, food security, homelessness, and public health
* Administrative experience overseeing budgets, compliance protocols, program development initiatives, and organizational policies
* Multilingual abilities are highly desirable
* Knowledge of Bay Area philanthropic networks, local family trusts are highly desirable
* Excellent writing and presentation skills

Pay: $100,000\.00 \- $110,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Health insurance
* Retirement plan

Education:

* Bachelor's (Required)

Experience:

* Senior leadership: 3 years (Required)

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Director of Development and Communications - GLBT Historical Society
jobs.description:
The GLBT Historical Society is a 501(c)3 nonprofit organization that collects, preserves, exhibits and makes accessible to the public materials and knowledge to support and promote understanding of LGBTQ history, culture, and arts in all their diversity. Founded in 1985, we are recognized internationally as a leader in the field of LGBTQ public history. We steward and make accessible one of the world’s largest repositories of LGBT historical materials through our archives, and we operate the nation’s first museum of LGBT History and Culture in San Francisco.

POSITION DESCRIPTION

The Director of Development and Communications is a key leadership position within our organization that leads our fundraising efforts and effectively communicates our mission and impact to stakeholders. The position will be critical in advancing the organization’s fundraising goals, cultivating donor relationships, and raising awareness of our work through strategic communication initiatives. Reporting directly to the Executive Director and supervising the Development Associate and the Marketing and Communications Manager, this role requires a dynamic individual with a strong background in all aspects of fundraising. This position will join the Society during an exciting moment of expansion and will play an important role in sustaining operations, planning for growth and leading a capital campaign.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

**Fundraising Strategy and Execution**

* Develop, refine and and implement comprehensive fundraising strategies to achieve revenue goals.
* In partnership with the Executive Director, Board, Program Directors, and Volunteer fundraisers, identify and cultivate relationships with individual donors, corporate sponsors, foundations, government agencies and other potential funding sources.
* Oversee and engage in grant writing and reporting processes, ensuring timely submissions and compliance with funder requirements.

**Donor Relations and Stewardship**

* Oversee and implement strategies to recognize and acknowledge donor contributions effectively.
* Regularly communicate with donors to provide updates on the organization’s impact and maintain donor engagement.
* Supervise staff engaged in various administrative tasks that support fund development, such as processing donations, generating acknowledgment letters, writing thank\-you notes, data entry, and other tasks.

**Communications Strategy and Brand Management**

* In partnership with the Marketing and Communications Manager, develop and implement a comprehensive communications strategy to effectively communicate the organization’s mission, programs, and impact.
* Supervise staff engaged in creating compelling content for various communications channels, including website, social media, e\-mail newsletters, and press releases.
* Ensure the organization’s brand identity is consistent across all communication materials.
* Support the Executive Director in responding to media inquiries and support the Marketing and Communications Manager in seeking opportunities for media coverage.

**Leadership** 

* Provide leadership, supervision, and guidance to staff and volunteers to achieve departmental goals.
* Support the Board of Directors and Board Development Committee in engaging in fundraising, cultivation, stewardship, and event planning.
* Serve as a member of the Society’s leadership team; collaborate with other Society operations and program teams.
* Develop and manage the fundraising and communications team budget.
* Work with capital campaign consultants in planning and implementing a multi\-year capital campaign.
* Manage donor database and oversee communications tools.
* Foster a culture of inclusivity, diversity, and equity throughout the organization’s fundraising efforts.

QUALIFICATIONS

* Minimum of 7 years of experience in fundraising roles within the nonprofit sector; previous director\-level experience preferred.
* At least three years of staff supervision experience preferred.

* Proficiency in using fundraising software and donor databases is required. Experience with Salesforce is preferred, and strong computer skills, such as Windows, Microsoft Office (Word, Excel), and Google Workspace, are required.
* Excellent leadership, supervision, and team\-building skills, with the ability to motivate and inspire staff, volunteers, interns, and stakeholders.
* Ability to work collaboratively in a fast\-paced environment and adapt to changing priorities. Excellent time\-management skills with the ability to plan, organize, and prioritize workload and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
* Experience working with LGBTQ\+ and diverse communities is preferred; a commitment to and proven track record in advancing justice, equity, diversity, inclusion, and accessibility in all aspects of fundraising and organizational practices is required.

PHYSICAL ABILITIES

* Ability to communicate via phone, video calls, and e\-mail
* Ability to lift and carry 25 pounds
* Ability to sit or stand for extended periods.

**About YCS**



Youth Consultation Service (YCS) is a mission\-driven nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting children, families, and communities through behavioral health, educational, and social service programs. **Position Summary**



YCS is seeking a strategic and experienced **Director of Grants Strategy \& Management** to lead and grow the organization’s enterprise\-wide grant funding efforts. This role serves as the primary authority for all grant\-related initiatives across YCS systems and is responsible for developing, writing, managing, and tracking a comprehensive grants portfolio aligned with organizational priorities and program impact goals.

**Qualifications:**


* Bachelor’s degree required in Nonprofit Management, Communications, Public Administration, Social Services, English, or related field

jobs.description:
**Organization Overview**


The School of American Ballet (SAB) at Lincoln Center, founded by George Balanchine and Lincoln Kirstein, is the preeminent ballet school in the country. Our mission is to train professional dancers for careers in classical ballet. We provide the resources for a diverse pool of students to train at the highest level – with 15\-25 a year going on to dance for New York City Ballet, our official but independent ballet company, and other major ballet companies worldwide. SAB has a far\-reaching impact on the art form and enriches the lives of each student who comes through its doors, over 800 annually, ages 6 to 18\. SAB has approximately 90 part\- and full\-time employees and an operating budget of $17 million. In the 2025\-2026 school year, administrative employees are expected to work in person 4 days per week and may telecommute one day per work week.

**Position Overview**


The School of American Ballet (SAB) seeks a Director of Institutional Giving to lead and expand its robust institutional giving program, comprised of foundation, government, and corporate foundation giving components. As a member of the School’s development staff, the Director of Institutional Giving will be responsible for raising over $1\.5 million annually, plus additional capital and endowment fundraising as needed. This position leads and grows the School's institutional fundraising and is a leader and resource for department\-wide staff and volunteers. The Director of Institutional Giving directly supervises and mentors one staff member. This is a full\-time, exempt position reporting to the Chief Development and Marketing Officer.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Institutional Giving**

* Manage and expand the School’s institutional giving strategy to secure more than $1\.5 million, with gifts ranging from $1,000 to $250,000\+.
* Build and manage relationships with 40\+ foundations, corporate, and government donors to ensure strong engagement with SAB and steward lasting support.
* Identify and strategically cultivate institutional prospects; implement tailored engagement strategies; solicit and secure gifts personally and as part of a team; and steward donors to maintain and strengthen long\-term relationships.
* Work closely with SAB\-wide staff to conceive of and submit persuasive, well\-written, and applicable proposals and reports, with accompanying budgets and support materials, on behalf of student life programming, the scholarship fund, and other priority initiatives.
* Oversee a comprehensive donor communication strategy, ensuring timely and high\-quality engagement through acknowledgement letters, written correspondence, invitations, mailings, visits, calls, newsletters, and e\-blasts.
* Develop strong relationships with Board members and coworkers; engage the Board’s Development Committee in cultivating and stewarding institutional donors; and serve as a resource to the Board and senior leadership team in their fundraising efforts.
* Guide prospect solicitation and donor stewardship efforts by the Executive Director and Board through the preparation of research, talking points, email drafts, and meeting briefings.
* Partner on the planning, execution, and fundraising for future capital and endowment campaigns.

**Supervision**

* Mentor, train, and supervise staff in Institutional Giving to ensure that departmental goals and needs are being met, and that staff are continually developing in their roles.
* Oversee the work conducted on behalf of Institutional Giving by department staff and volunteers.
* Supervise the maintenance of tracking systems, Institutional Giving mailing lists, and electronic and physical donor records.
* Manage Institutional Giving’s expense budget.

  

**Requirements** **Qualifications**

* 5\+ years of demonstrated success in institutional giving; knowledge of New York area funders.
* Excellent written and oral communication skills; fluency in budgeting and data analysis; ability to manage time and projects in a fast\-paced environment.
* Proven track record of securing institutional gifts at the $100,000\+ level.
* Polished and professional demeanor, with the ability to speak on behalf of the School at events.
* Proficiency in Raiser’s Edge or a similar donor database.
* Tasks might include some lifting, including heavy items that require use of carts.
* Evening and weekend hours required for donor events.

  

**Benefits**  

SAB offers a superior benefit package, including full health benefits, four weeks of vacation (plus two holiday weeks in December), and generous retirement savings benefits.


The School of American Ballet is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Diverse candidates are encouraged to apply.


The annual salary range is $100,000\-$112,000\.

The National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) is one of the fastest\-growing professional sports leagues in the U.S., powered by 16 clubs and a deep roster of the world’s best players, and built on record\-shattering fan, media and commercial growth. Now in its 14th season, the league’s momentum continues to accelerate, with viewership and attendance numbers growing rapidly, social media fandom on the rise, team valuations massively increasing and new top sponsors investing in the NWSL brand. This unprecedented growth in audience, media reach, and franchise value reflects the NWSL’s expanding fan base and increasing dominance in the sports\-media landscape and popular culture.

  

The future of the NWSL is now — and we’re looking for world\-class talent like you to help us continue the momentum.

 **About the NWSL Foundation**


The NWSL Foundation exists to advance the health and longevity of women athletes by supporting women’s health research and convening and coordinating the women’s athletic health research ecosystem. The Executive Director must be equally comfortable engaging senior researchers and clinicians, league and club leadership, players, and donors. This role requires judgment, credibility, and the ability to direct complex, multi\-stakeholder conversations—not simply administer programs.

**Company Description** **Beginnings Fund**


POSITION: Director of Communications and Strategic Partnerships


REPORTS TO: CEO, Beginnings Fund


FLSA STATUS: Full\-time, Exempt


SALARY RANGE: $120,000 \- $160,000 USD


LOCATION: Remote – New York, London or Nairobi


WEBSITE: https://www.beginningsfund.org

 **Background**


Every year in Africa, 182,000 mothers die from preventable pregnancy\- and childbirth\-related causes, 950,000 babies are stillborn, and 1\.2 million newborns die. Global progress against maternal and newborn mortality has stalled in recent years, and most African countries are not on track to meet the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals for maternal and newborn survival.


The Beginnings Fund is a philanthropic initiative that accelerates maternal and newborn survival in Africa by investing, in partnership with governments, in the products, people, and systems needed to sustainably improve care at scale. During its first five years, the Beginnings Fund will focus on Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Ghana, Lesotho, Uganda, and Zimbabwe. Investments are developed and managed by a majority\-Africa\-based Investment Team, led by a Nairobi\-based CEO who reports to an Investment Committee composed of the founding and anchor investors in the Beginnings Fund.


While the fund's initial phase is five years, the broader ambition is to raise $1 billion over ten years to expand into additional countries, with the potential to grow into a long\-term collaborative fund.


The Beginnings Fund is fiscally sponsored by Global Impact.

The Muhammad Ali Center was created to honor the life of “The Greatest”. Based in Louisville, KY, the Center is a multicultural organization, an award\-winning museum, and a global beacon for social justice. We exist to mobilize Ali’s legacy to foster respect, inspire generations of changemakers, and advance social justice, creating a world where all people can achieve their own greatness.

From the Ali Center's inception, Diversity, Equity, \& Inclusion have been central to our core values. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer that believes diverse viewpoints are critical to our global impact, and we actively foster a culture where inclusion is everyone’s responsibility.

**POSITION OVERVIEW:**

The President \& Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will provide the visionary leadership, strategic direction, and operational oversight required to champion the Ali Center’s mission and drive its next phase of global growth. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CEO holds full executive authority and accountability for all Center operations, including a $5M operating budget, a dedicated team of 30\+ staff and volunteers, programming and the operations of our world\-class facility.

As a primary public face of the Center, the CEO will convert mission into measurable global results. A proven track record of high\-level fundraising is paramount; the CEO will spearhead philanthropic growth across individual, corporate, foundational, and government sectors to ensure long\-term financial sustainability.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES** 

**Strategic Leadership \& Brand Advocacy** 

· **Drive Vision \& Growth**: Lead the execution of the strategic plan, aligning operational goals, revenue development, and programming with the Center’s core values.

· **Global Vision \& Expansion**: Drive the strategy to elevate the Center’s national and international profile. Collaborate closely with the senior leadership team to strategically cultivate relationships with major donors, community leaders, and global partners, positioning the Center for broad geographic and philanthropic growth.

**Revenue Generation \& Sustainability** 

· **Capital Cultivation**: Personally initiate and lead major fundraising campaigns, with a proven ability to close gifts at the 6\-figure (required) and 7\-figure (preferred) levels.

· **Diversify Revenue**: Expand funding streams through corporate partnerships, licensing, institutional grants, and strategic monetization of the Center’s assets.

**Operational Excellence \& Culture**

· **People \& Culture**: Inspire, mentor, and retain a high\-performing, diverse team, fostering a collaborative, respectful, and mission\-driven workplace culture.

· **Impact Measurement**: Establish rigorous evaluation frameworks to assess programming efficacy, ensuring initiatives remain impactful, sustainable, and tied to the mission.

· **Board Partnership**: Maintain transparent, regular, and strategic communications with the Board of Directors to optimize governance and organizational health.

**PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE \& QUALIFICATIONS** 

The ideal candidate is a visionary, energetic, and collaborative leader who pair executive acumen with the empathy, kindness, and welcoming spirit modeled by Muhammad Ali.

**REQUIRED EXPERIENCE:**

· **Executive Leadership**: A minimum of 10 years of progressive leadership experience in high\-profile nonprofits, NGOs, educational institutions, foundations, or corporate entities.

· **Fundraising Excellence**: A documented history of securing major gifts and scaling philanthropic revenue from diverse donor networks.

· **Business \& Fiscal Acumen**: Proven experience managing multi\-million dollar budgets, with a strong sensitivity to expense management and a track record of driving balance financial performance.

· **Partnership \& Alliance Building**: Skilled at building consensus among diverse stakeholders, including board members, elected officials, community leaders, and international partners.

· **Governance**: Proven success collaborating with and leveraging a highly engaged Board of Directors.

**About the Council Bluffs Schools Foundation:** The Council Bluffs Schools Foundation is a nonprofit 501c3 organization, governed by a board of directors, which provides financial resources and support to benefit the children, families, and staff of the Council Bluffs Community School District.

In pursuit of our mission, the foundation operates three signature programs:

* Kids \& Company is a before and after school childcare program operating out of 10 elementary buildings in the Council Bluffs School District that provides supervision and engaging activities to more than 800 children.
* STARS Scholarship provides financial, social, and emotional support for adult, low\-income parents in Pottawattamie County as they pursue a postsecondary degree or career training certification.
* Alumni \& Friends aims to create a network of individuals who wish to support the school district, connect with old friends, and stay informed.

In addition to these programs, we administer high school scholarship funds, and provide opportunities for our community of donors to support education in Council Bluffs.

**POSITION SUMMARY:** The Director of Development is responsible for donor and alumni relations, and planning, organizing, and directing fundraising efforts of the foundation, including the major gifts program, annual fund, planned giving, grant writing, and special events. * Secure operational and program funding
* Increase alumni, donor, and community engagement.
* Improve the identity of the Foundation within the community.

* Create a development plan integrated with the strategic goals of the foundation that includes the annual campaign, major gifts, planned giving, events, and grants.

**About Amyloidosis Research Consortium**


The Amyloidosis Research Consortium (ARC) is a 501c(3\) nonprofit organization founded in 2015, harnessing the power of collaboration and innovation to advance science and both improve and extend the lives of those with Amyloidosis. We are dedicated to transforming the way research is being done and focus on what will have the most significant impact on improving the lives of amyloidosis patients. We forge collaborations across industry, research, clinical care, and regulatory to address unmet needs and accelerate the discovery of new treatments. ARC empowers and supports patients by ensuring they have access to the best quality care and information.

  

Amyloidosis is a group of diseases where abnormal proteins build up in organs, causing progressive damage. In the U.S., approximately 3,800 new AL amyloidosis cases are diagnosed annually. However, ATTR amyloidosis affects far more people: over 100,000 Americans have the age\-related form, and 50,000 people worldwide have the inherited form. Studies show that roughly 13% of older heart failure patients actually have undiagnosed ATTR amyloidosis, meaning the true patient population is even larger. As awareness and diagnosis improve, the community continues to grow.

**Type of Employment:** Exempt, Full\-Time


**Location:** Austin, Texas (Hybrid). This position is primarily community\-based and requires frequent in\-person outreach throughout Austin. The Program Director will spend a significant portion of their time visiting restaurants, bars, food trucks, and other food and beverage businesses to build relationships, recruit members, and support the Healthcare Access Program. This role offers a flexible schedule; however, evening and occasional weekend events are expected.


### **About Good Work Austin**


Good Work Austin (GWA) is the only nonprofit organization in Central Texas dedicated to better jobs and fair treatment for food \& beverage workers. Our mission is to foster healthy careers in the local food and beverage industry through professional development and advocacy for more equitable practices. GWA was created by food and beverage business owners and workers who came together to reimagine what stable, dignified employment could look like in an industry long plagued by low wages and limited mobility.


Today, GWA works with some of Austin's leading chefs and food businesses, strengthening the city's vibrant food scene while building a more sustainable and equitable industry. Through our Culinary Workforce Training, Community Kitchen, and Healthy Workplaces programs, we create opportunities for workers to learn new skills, for small businesses to thrive, and for the community to benefit from healthier, more just workplaces.


Our organizational culture reflects the values we champion: respect for each person's lived experience and life outside of work, and a balance of accountability and support. We live by our core values of Collaboration, Community, Integrity, Innovation, and Inclusion, working together with a spirit of creativity and care to create lasting change in Austin's food and beverage industry.


### **Purpose of the Position**


The Program Director role leads Good Work Austin's Healthcare Access Program while driving strategic growth of the organization's membership network. This position is responsible for overseeing healthcare access services for food and beverage workers, and strengthening partnerships across the healthcare and hospitality sectors while recruiting new food and beverage businesses and workers into Good Work Austin's membership community.


The ideal candidate is a natural relationship builder who enjoys connecting with new people, isn't afraid to walk into a restaurant and start a conversation, and is energized by helping grow a mission\-driven organization. We're looking for someone who thrives on building relationships, enjoys meeting new people every day, and is energized by being out in the community rather than sitting behind a desk.


Working closely with the Executive Director, the Program Director develops strategies that leverage healthcare access as an entry point for deeper engagement with Good Work Austin. By building relationships with workers, employers, and community partners, the Program Director helps expand participation across the organization's programs while advancing its mission to improve jobs and working conditions in the local food and beverage industry.


This position also oversees program evaluation, partnership management, grant reporting, and long\-term strategic planning to ensure the Healthcare Access Program continues to grow as a sustainable and impactful initiative.

* Develop and implement outreach strategies to increase awareness of Good Work Austin's programs and expand organizational membership.
* Serve as the primary point of contact for healthcare and community partners, including Central Health, Foundation Communities, Sendero Health Plans, healthcare providers, and other referral organizations.
* Represent Good Work Austin at community events, conferences, coalition meetings, and industry gatherings.

**Chief Executive Officer, Habitat for Humanity of the NC Sandhills**

Habitat for Humanity of the NC Sandhills is a large, rural affiliate in three counties dedicated to fostering strength, stability, and self\-reliance through affordable housing solutions. For 38 years of proven results, we have served more than 1,000 families by building 340\+ homes, completing 300\+ critical home repairs throughout the Sandhills.
